content.task_ref: Create Common Lisp Orchestrator SDK directory structure and ASDF system definition
content.summary: Created complete Common Lisp SDK directory structure and ASDF system definition for SW4RM Recursive Tree Orchestration Layer. The implementation includes a comprehensive package system with 8 subpackages organized by concern (tree, envelope, routing, errors, coordination, grpc, persistence), full configuration management system, main entry point with CLI support, and test infrastructure using FiveAM.

sections_implemented: COMMON_LISP_PLAN.md Part 5: Tooling - ASDF system dependencies
Package definitions follow Lisp conventions with comprehensive docstrings
deviations: gRPC dependencies (grpc, cl-protobuf) commented out in ASDF as they need custom integration - this is expected per plan
JSON configuration loading stubbed (requires cl-json integration)
Some platform-specific features (signal handlers, environment variables) use #+sbcl conditionals

asdf_system.name: sw4rm-orchestrator
asdf_system.load_order: Serial loading with proper dependency order: package -> config -> tree -> envelope -> routing -> errors -> coordination -> grpc -> persistence -> main

features: Hash-table based configuration with string keys
Multi-source loading: defaults, config file, environment, CLI, programmatic
Precedence order: programmatic > CLI > env > file > defaults
Load/save in Lisp and JSON formats
Configuration validation with type checking and range validation
Command-line argument parsing with help text
Multi-source initialization (checkpoint restore or fresh start)
Signal handler installation (SIGINT, SIGTERM for graceful shutdown)
Main event loop with shutdown coordination

content.testing_notes:
Test Engineer should focus on:
1. Verify ASDF system loads successfully in SBCL and CCL
2. Test configuration loading from all sources (file, env, CLI, programmatic)
3. Test configuration precedence order is correct
4. Verify CLI argument parsing handles all flags
5. Test graceful shutdown saves checkpoint correctly
6. Verify signal handlers work on different platforms
7. Once tree/envelope/routing modules are implemented, write comprehensive unit tests
8. Integration tests will require Python sw4rm instances running on specific ports
content.documentation_notes:
Technical Editor should document:
1. ASDF system architecture and dependency rationale
2. Package organization and why we have 8+ subpackages
3. Configuration system design and multi-source loading strategy
4. CLI usage examples for different deployment scenarios
5. REPL development workflow for interactive orchestrator development
6. How to build standalone executables
7. Signal handling and graceful shutdown semantics
8. Cross-reference with COMMON_LISP_PLAN.md for architectural context
